source: NCERT Class VIII, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 12.

sections.heading: 1. The Ecosystem
points: An **ecosystem** = a community of **living organisms (biotic)** interacting with their **non-living (abiotic)** surroundings.
**Biotic components:** producers, consumers, decomposers; **abiotic:** air, water, soil, sunlight, temperature.
All parts are **interdependent** — a change in one affects the whole.

sections.heading: 2. Food Chains and Food Webs
points: **Producers** (green plants) make food; **consumers** (herbivores, carnivores) eat others; **decomposers** (microbes, fungi) break down dead matter.
A **food chain** shows who eats whom: e.g. **grass → grasshopper → frog → snake**.
Many interlinked chains form a **food web**.
Energy flows from the Sun → producers → consumers; only a **small fraction** passes to each next level.

sections.heading: 3. Cycles in Nature
points: Nature **recycles** materials through cycles:

sub: **Oxygen–carbon dioxide cycle** — plants release O₂ (photosynthesis), all organisms release CO₂ (respiration).
**Nitrogen cycle** — nitrogen fixed by bacteria/lightning → plants → animals → decomposers → back to air.

points: These cycles keep nature in **balance**.

sections.heading: 4. Balance of Nature and its Disturbance
points: Human activities — **deforestation, pollution, overuse of resources** — disturb the balance and harm ecosystems.
Loss of one species affects many others through the food web.
**Conservation** and sustainable use are needed to keep nature in harmony.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Ecosystem = biotic (living) + abiotic (non-living) interacting; interdependent.
Producers → consumers → decomposers; food chain (grass→grasshopper→frog→snake) → food web.
Energy flows from Sun → producers → consumers (only a little to each next level).
Cycles: water, oxygen–carbon dioxide, nitrogen — recycle materials.
Human activity (deforestation, pollution) disturbs the balance of nature.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: In a food chain, the **arrow points from the eaten to the eater** (grass → grasshopper → frog).
**Decomposers** recycle nutrients; without them, dead matter would pile up.
**Energy decreases** at each higher level of a food chain.
Ecosystems include **both** living and non-living parts.
